Claiming succeeds UNCHANGED from all four admitting statuses: the lease is issued, the Execution created, the fencing token non-zero, the Increment version advanced by one, the increment.claimed event recorded and the claim-issued outbox item staged. Every fixture that passed because the question was not asked now NAMES, as a domain constant literal at its seeding site, the status it establishes. internal/runner/orchestrator.go's RunFakeJourney reaches `ready` through the product's own Service.StartFraming and V2-084's Service.CompleteFraming rather than a store write, which is this task's only reachability proof. V2-090's pause now actually stops new claims (docs/product/definition.md:143 '新しい仕事のclaimを止める'), and V2-084's F1 is closed for the cancelled case. ROW 2 -- WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO. internal/domain/** is PROHIBITED and byte-unchanged: no RequirementStatus is added, no RequirementCommandKind, and internal/domain/model.go:486's allowed(RequirementReady, RequirementRecovering, RequirementWaiting) is not widened -- which is precisely what makes admitting `captured` a build failure rather than a decision. Service.Renew is NOT touched: internal/application/service.go:284-288 keeps asking only the needs-input question, and a lease already held is neither revoked nor refused renewal when its parent leaves the admitting set. No lease is expired, no Execution terminated. Service.Plan and Service.Prepare are NOT refused. No port is added; no openapi path, response code or schema is added (contracts/** is PROHIBITED and contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml already declares '409' among claims:acquire's responses -- MEASURED at :144, the single-line responses map; the Work Order says :144-149), so contracts_changed is EMPTY, the contracts evidence key does not move and this task does not enrol in the api-contract chain. nextAction changes by not one byte: internal/application/readmodels.go and readmodels_test.go are PROHIBITED. requirementAwaitsHumanInput is NOT widened and ErrAwaitingHumanInput is NOT reused: internal/application/human_input.go and human_input_test.go are PROHIBITED. docs/** is PROHIBITED, so no product text is added. ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are untouched; this change creates and removes NO component import edge. ROW 3 -- WHAT IT RECORDS BUT DOES NOT FIX. (a) An Increment can still be PLANNED and PREPARED under a Requirement that admits no work, because Service.Plan writes the parent without a domain command (MEASURED: the SaveRequirement call inside Service.Plan). Recorded, never asserted, never fixed here. (b) internal/application/readmodels.go's nextAction still reports 'run next increment' for a ready Increment whose parent admits nothing, so the read model advertises an action the claim now refuses; readmodels.go is held by another task. (c) A claim from waiting or recovering SUCCEEDS and leaves the parent in waiting or recovering, because V2-084's parent transition fires only from ready, so the aggregate still contradicts docs/architecture/domain-model.md:266's definition of `active`. (d) The TWO cells where docs/architecture/domain-model.md is WIDER than internal/domain: :268 lists `active` among needs-input's 主な遷移先 and :271 lists `active` among evaluating's, while internal/domain/model.go:486 admits RequirementStart from neither. Logged as a named finding for the tech_lead and asserted NOWHERE, for the reason internal/application/framing_test.go already gives -- asserting a defect pins it in place. (e) A lease already held is not revoked when the parent leaves the admitting set. (f) internal/store/firestore's suite prints ok while skipping everything without an emulator; the skip figure is recorded WITH ITS PATTERN and never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). No new task id is proposed: M5's remediation budget is at 5 of 5 (§12.7), and every finding above is a row of THIS table. ROW 4 -- WHAT ONLY A LATER TASK CAN ESTABLISH. That a refusal stops work already in flight, which needs the propagation and the stop-completion observation docs/product/definition.md:164 defines. That `waiting` and `recovering` are journey-reachable, which needs non-test issuers for domain.RequirementWait and domain.RequirementRecover -- MEASURED to have ZERO issuers.
